english.title: Aid, abet, counsel and procure the destruction of / damage to property valued over £5000
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), aided, abetted, counselled and procured **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) without lawful excuse to,

(A)_[destroy **(..SPECIFY THE PROPERTY..)]_
(B)_[damage **(..SPECIFY THE PROPERTY..)]_

to the value of **(..SPECIFY THE VALUE OVER FIVE THOUSAND POUNDS..) belonging to **(..SPECIFY THE NAME..) intending to destroy or damage such property or being reckless as to whether such property would be destroyed or damaged
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 1(1) and 4 of the Criminal Damage Act 1971 and section 8 of the Accessories and Abettors Act 1861.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) See offence wordingH2081 for the substantive offence and H2082 - where the damage involved is less than five thousand pounds in value.
(ii) Property damaged / destroyed must not belong to defendant(s).
(iii) Consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions is required where damage is to spouse's property (section 30(4) of the Theft Act 1968).
(iv) The same incident may involve separate activities, some causing ordinary damage and some damage by fire (for example, protestors break into a laboratory building, smash laboratory equipment and set fire to some files). In such circumstances they are separate offences and best charged as such (R v Booth 1999).

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Ten years imprisonment.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
